title: Universal thermal breakdown of polaron coherence in one, two, and three dimensions
authors: Jeet Shannigrahi, Janez Bonča, Mona Berciu
abstract: How a polaron loses its quasiparticle coherence with increasing temperature is a long-standing open problem. Holstein addressed it in 1959 only in the extreme antiadiabatic, strong-coupling limit, while more recent numerically exact approaches are largely restricted to one dimension. Here we solve this problem on square and simple cubic lattices across the weak-, intermediate-, and strong-coupling regimes. We show that the polaron effective mass $m^*$ and inverse lifetime $1/τ$ increase monotonically with temperature until, at $T \sim 0.5\,Ω$, the quasiparticle peak dissolves into a broad incoherent thermal continuum. The phonon frequency $Ω$ therefore defines a universal coherence scale, independent of dimensionality and coupling strength, validating Holstein's prediction far beyond the regime in which it was derived. These results follow from a finite-temperature generalization of the Momentum Average (MA) approximation, yielding a closed-form, diagrammatically derived self-energy that is asymptotically exact in the strong-coupling limit at all temperatures. Benchmark comparisons demonstrate excellent quantitative agreement of the resulting 1D spectral functions with the numerically exact Variational Exact Diagonalization-Finite-Temperature Lanczos Method (VED-FTLM) and finite-$T$ Density Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG).
summary: This work tackles the thermal decoherence of polarons using an advanced, diagrammatically derived approximation (MA). The authors demonstrate that polaron coherence universally breaks down at a temperature scale set by the phonon frequency, validating theoretical predictions across 1D, 2D, and 3D systems. The method shows excellent quantitative agreement with state-of-the-art numerical techniques.
main_problem: The paper addresses the long-standing open problem of how polaron quasiparticle coherence degrades as temperature increases.
main_result: The coherence breakdown is universal, occurring when the quasiparticle peak dissolves into a broad thermal continuum at a temperature scale set by the phonon frequency $\Omega$, independent of dimensionality or coupling strength.
method: The authors employ a finite-temperature generalization of the Momentum Average (MA) approximation, yielding a diagrammatically derived self-energy.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by the Holstein Hamiltonian, describing a polaron (electron coupled to phonons) hopping on a hyper-cubic lattice in 1D, 2D, and 3D.
key_observables: Polaron effective mass ($m^*$), inverse lifetime ($1/\tau$), and the spectral function $A(\omega, k)$.
important_parameters: Temperature ($T$), phonon frequency ($\Omega$), coupling strength ($\lambda$), and dimensionality ($D=1, 2, 3$).
main_assumptions: The MA framework uses an ansatz (MA(0) or MA(1)) that is asymptotically exact in the strong-coupling limit at all temperatures.
figures_summary: Figures compare the temperature dependence of $m^*$ and broadening ($\eta^*$) across dimensions and couplings, and show spectral function evolution comparing MA results against benchmark methods like VED-FTLM and DMRG.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the MA approximation, compares its results against established numerical benchmarks (VED-FTLM, DMRG, DMFT), and analyzes the temperature dependence of coherence loss across various coupling and dimensional regimes.
why_interesting: The universal coherence scale defined by $\Omega$ provides a robust theoretical prediction for polaron dynamics that transcends the restrictive limits of previous theoretical treatments, connecting fundamental lattice models to observable thermal behavior.
